extracted.intended_audience: public health risk communicators, emergency response professionals, national and local health authorities, policy makers, and partners (PAHO/WHO region)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and delivering real-time risk and outbreak communication to enable affected populations to make informed decisions, including building national capacity, coordinating partners, managing misinformation, and engaging communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and ultimate goal of risk communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication is the real-time exchange of information, recommendations, and opinions between experts and/or officials and people who face a threat (risk) to their survival, health, or economic or social well-being. The ultimate goal of risk communication is that every person exposed to a risk is able to make informed decisions to mitigate the effects of the threat and take protective and preventive measures and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on real-time exchange; messaging should enable individuals to understand the threat and take protective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider political, social and economic factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communications takes into consideration political, social and economic factors; analyzes risk and risk perception to communicate effectively; and gives great importance to dialogue with affected and targeted populations to help them make the best possible decisions during public health emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of context (political/social/economic) and perceptions should shape messaging and approach; prioritize dialogue rather than one-way information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand stakeholders' perceptions, concerns and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication requires an understanding of stakeholders' perceptions, concerns, and beliefs, as well as their knowledge and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather and use information on audience beliefs and practices to tailor messages and interventions; listening is as important as message delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and manage rumors and misinformation from the outset
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective risk communication must be able to identify and be able to handle rumors, as well as misinformation and other communication challenges from the outset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively detect, track and address misinformation and rumors early in the response to reduce harm and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust as a precondition
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication only works when there is communication based on trust between those with the knowledge (experts), those in charge (authorities), and those affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build and maintain trust through consistent, honest communication and by demonstrating care and empathy; without trust, people are unlikely to follow recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening and two-way dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Listening to and understanding people's beliefs, concerns and perceptions is as important as providing them with evidence and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate mechanisms for listening (surveys, community engagement, feedback channels) and respond to concerns rather than only broadcasting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Honestly explaining what is known about the nature of the risk and admitting what is uncertain is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about uncertainties and limitations of knowledge to preserve credibility; avoid overconfidence or withholding relevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility, empathy and identification with the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The credibility of those giving information and recommendations; their expressions of caring and empathy, as well as identification with the audience are factors that make risk communication effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicators should demonstrate empathy, show understanding of affected populations, and present information through trusted messengers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate quickly and frequently
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate to the public quickly and frequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize rapid, regular updates to reduce speculation and information vacuums; frequency helps maintain relevance and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate with transparency and honesty (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate with transparency and honesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure messages are truthful, complete where possible, and acknowledge limits of knowledge; align with institutional transparency policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate even in the midst of uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate even in the midst of uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not wait for perfect information; explain current knowledge and how it may evolve. Use clear statements about what is known and unknown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show empathy, solidarity and understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Show empathy, solidarity and understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use compassionate language, acknowledge hardships, and demonstrate solidarity with affected communities to foster trust and adherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Involve communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage community leaders, organizations and members in planning and dissemination to ensure relevance and acceptance of messages and interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a comprehensive approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a comprehensive approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine risk communication with community engagement, social science inputs, infodemic management, and other relevant disciplines for a holistic response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate with one voice: coordinate with partners and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate with one voice: coordinate with partners and other stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align messages across agencies and partners to avoid conflicting guidance; establish coordination mechanisms and agreed messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen and respond to public concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen and respond to public concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively solicit feedback and respond publicly to concerns to show responsiveness and adjust strategies as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to national capacity building
rubrics_metrics.description: Contribute to the national capacity building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support the development of national policies, strategies and workforce to sustain risk communication capabilities over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish policy, strategy and plans for risk communication
rubrics_metrics.description: WHO is supporting countries to build capacity by establishing the right policy, strategy, and plans for risk communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop formal policies, strategic plans and operational plans that define roles, responsibilities, resources and processes for risk communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train key staff and journalists on health emergency reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Training key staff, involving and training journalists on how to report on health emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide targeted training for public health communicators and media professionals to improve quality, accuracy and sensitivity of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run simulation exercises to test national systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Running simulation exercises to test national systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct exercises and drills to validate communication plans, coordination, and information flows before real emergencies occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deploy risk communication personnel during responses
rubrics_metrics.description: In emergency situations, WHO provides support by deploying its network of risk communicators to affected countries and regions to work side by side with national and local authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure rapid deployment of skilled communicators to support local capacity, message development, community engagement, and coordination during crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat risk communication as a core capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of risk communication as a capability on par with epidemiology and provision of healthcare, through strategies that minimize risks and empower communities to make evidence-based decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate comparable status, resources and institutional attention to risk communication as to epidemiology and clinical care in preparedness planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infodemic management: understand and identify mechanisms and actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding and identifying its key mechanisms and actors. This course is for anyone interested in understanding what an infodemic is, how it dramatically affects public health and what we can do about it now and into the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include infodemic management in communication strategies: map information ecosystems, actors, and channels; design interventions to reduce spread of harmful misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply community engagement and social science operational concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: An overview of operational concepts in relation to community engagement, risk communication, and the application of social science interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social science methods to inform engagement strategies, adapt interventions to cultural contexts, and empower communities before, during and after outbreaks.
